title: Intrinsic Orbital Hall Effect in Degenerate Spin-3/2 Systems driven by the quantum metric
abstract: We show that in rotationally invariant spin-$3/2$ systems the orbital Hall effect originates from interband matrix elements of the orbital magnetic moment. The resulting Hall response is governed by the quantum metric, rather than by the Berry curvature, revealing a purely geometric transport mechanism. Conventional intraband contributions associated with the orbital magnetic moment and Berry curvature are shown to vanish identically in degenerate systems. These results identify the quantum metric as the key geometric quantity controlling orbital Hall transport in degenerate multiband systems.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the intrinsic Orbital Hall Effect in spin-3/2 degenerate semiconductors. It proves that this effect is not due to the Berry curvature, but rather arises purely from interband contributions mediated by the quantum metric. This establishes a distinct, geometrically controlled mechanism for orbital transport.
main_problem: The study investigates the intrinsic Orbital Hall Effect (OHE) in degenerate spin-3/2 systems to determine the fundamental geometric quantity governing this transport.
main_result: The OHE is found to be governed entirely by the quantum metric acting on interband orbital magnetic moment components, rather than the Berry curvature or conventional intraband contributions.
method: Theoretical calculation using linear response theory applied to a Luttinger Hamiltonian model, focusing on matrix elements of the Orbital Magnetic Moment (OMM).
model_or_system: The system is modeled as degenerate spin-3/2 semiconductors described by a Luttinger Hamiltonian. The analysis leverages symmetries inherent in this degenerate manifold.
key_observables: Orbital Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{z,	ext{Hall}}^{yx}$), Orbital Magnetic Moment (OMM), Quantum Metric components ($g_{xx}, g_{yx}$).
important_parameters: Fermi energy ($\epsilon_F$), material parameters related to heavy-hole and light-hole band gaps ($\gamma_{3/2} - \gamma_{1/2}$), and the Luttinger Hamiltonian coefficients.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes rotational invariance, utilizes the Luttinger model framework, and relies on approximations like the spherical approximation for tractability.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic dispersion relations comparing linear and quadratic Hamiltonians, showing where intraband OMM vanishes in the degenerate spectrum. Contour plots visualize momentum-space distributions of the quantum metric components.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem by noting that conventional contributions vanish in degenerate systems. It then develops the theory to show the survival of an interband mechanism governed solely by the quantum metric, culminating in explicit analytical expressions and numerical estimates for various semiconductors.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the reliance on 'quantum geometry' (the quantum metric) as a primary physical observable connects directly to geometric phases and topological invariants studied in AMO physics.
